title: Completion pullback normalized on quotient projections
statement: Let $a:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with $Y$ Noetherian, $J\subset\mathcal O_Y$ an ideal sheaf and $F$ a coherent module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, pqf-def-coherent, def-pc-module-pullback]. Suppose $I=J.\operatorname{comap}(a)$ and a module $M$ on $X$ is supplied with $h_M:M=a^*F$. There exists an isomorphism $e:a^*(F^{\wedge}_J)\simeq M^{\wedge}_I$ of inverse systems, and for every level $n$ the pulled quotient projection followed by $e_n$ is $h_M^{-1}$ followed by the quotient projection $M\to M/I^{n+1}M$. The normalization specifies the quotient comparison on all levels.

source.place: Proof, pullback of ideal-power quotients; completion identity in the proof of 088B

proof.text: Eliminate the supplied ideal and module equalities. Take the inverse of completionPullbackIso at F, from the existing formal-system pullback construction. Its component at n is the inverse powerQuotientIso. The existing powerQuotientIso projection equation says that the new quotient projection followed by its forward comparison is a* of the original projection. Postcompose with its inverse and cancel the isomorphism. This proves exactly the normalized equation. Naturality and compatibility with transitions are already part of completionPullbackIso. Pulled quotient projections are epimorphisms because pullback is a left adjoint, so the normalization determines the comparison uniquely; no arbitrary data is selected. Zero modules, zero/unit ideals and empty schemes use the same equations.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_formalCompletionPullback_normalized
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y] (a : X ⟶ Y) (J : Y.IdealSheafData)
    (F : CoherentModules Y) (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : J.comap a = I)
    (M : X.Modules) (hM : M = (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback a).obj F.obj) :
    ∃ e : formalCompletionSystem J F.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback a ≅
        formalCompletionSystem I M,
      ∀ n : ℕ, (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback a).map
          (formalModuleQuotientπ J (n + 1) F.obj) ≫ e.hom.app (op n) =
        eqToHom hM.symm ≫ formalModuleQuotientπ I (n + 1) M
